reviewers.R1: Prüferin (licensed Goethe-Zertifikat A2 examiner persona): exam fidelity, rubric application, task clarity
reviewers.R2: Kursleiterin DaF/DaZ at A2.1: naturalness, level, didactics, scene plausibility

scope: content/course-v2/a2.1/units/u04.json (every German string, every item solved blind)
docs/course-v2/curriculum/a2-1.md E4; research/01-exams-a1-a2.md (Goethe A2 task shapes); BLUEPRINT §4.9, §9.4, §9.5
method: The unit parses. scripts/course-v2/check.mjs reports 0 errors. scripts/course-v2/validate.mjs reports FAIL: 2 blockers, both in the a2.1 lexicon rather than in this unit (LEX-07), 28 LEX-02 ratchet warnings and 5 advisories (GRM-04 x4, TXT-03 x1). All are listed below. All 93 items (start gist, 15 input items, 12 structured-input items, 45 pool/reserve items, 9 exam items, 8 check items and 3 proof items) were solved blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line only. Keys were checked against the texts and accepted[] against defensible alternatives. Exam blocks were compared with ga2.json and with the Goethe A2 task shapes in memo 01. The grammar ceiling was checked by script: definite article + adjective (u05), nullartikel (a2.2), attributive comparison (a2.2), jeden + accusative (u07), sollen (a1.2), imperative du (a1.2). Cast and story facts were compared with casts/a2.json and series.json.
verdict: The unit is well built. The German is correct throughout, the story is lively and coherent (no coffee → shop → comparison → wrong parcel → complaint, with a cliffhanger that feeds E5), the adjective-ending and indefinite-pronoun drills are dense and correctly keyed, and the Hören-3 and Schreiben-2 tasks are original and on format. No item key is wrong. The unit is not ready to exit. Seven unit-level MAJORs remain: the Sprechen Teil 1 cards use a themed layout that Goethe A2 Sp1 does not have; the pictorial Hören-3 block is not flagged as its text variant; the Wegweiser is about a third of the planned length; a strategy card gives away an exam item's answer; one can-do (alltagsdinge-bewerten) is never really rehearsed; and three items have a defensible second answer. The two LEX-07 blockers belong to the a2.1 lexicon, not this unit, but they fail the validator run on this file.

findings.quote: „Leitung“ (NOUN) is entered more than once (b1.1:lx.leitung-2) with different glosses: line (telephone) | management; (team) leadership
findings.problem: LEX-07 blocker from the validator run on u04. The homograph needs its own id, and until it has one the file fails validation.
findings.fix: Give the second sense its own id, lx.leitung-2, in the lexicon where it is introduced, or merge the glosses if it is one lemma. The lexicon owner makes this change; u04 is not touched.

findings.quote: „Tafel“ (NOUN) is entered more than once (b1.2:lx.tafel-2) with different glosses: board (in a classroom) | food bank
findings.problem: LEX-07 blocker from the validator run on u04. Same homograph-id issue as lx.leitung.
findings.fix: Use lx.tafel-2 for the food-bank sense. The lexicon owner makes this change.

findings.quote: „Sprechen Teil 1: Sie und Ihre Partnerin haben je vier Karten zum Thema „Einkaufen“.“ · „Einkaufen: Supermarkt?“, „Einkaufen: Marke?“ …
findings.problem: Goethe A2 Sprechen Teil 1 is „Fragen zur Person“: each card carries a single personal keyword (e.g. „Wohnort?“ → „Wo wohnen Sie?“; memo 01, US-A2 S. 23–24, ga2.sp1 source). It has no topic and no „Thema:“ header. The themed card layout („Einkaufen: …?“) belongs to Start Deutsch 1 Teil 2 and telc A2 Sprechen Teil 2 (the plan's original lane). The task is labelled ga2.sp1 but rehearses the card format of another exam. A learner will expect a topic header in the Goethe exam and phrase topic questions instead of questions about the partner's person.
findings.fix: Make situationDe „Sprechen Teil 1: Fragen zur Person. Sie und Ihre Partnerin haben je vier Karten.“ Use bare keyword cards that can be asked as personal questions and stay close to the unit, e.g. learner: „Einkaufen?“, „Internet?“, „Geschenk?“, „Küche?“; partner: „Samstag?“, „Kaufhaus?“, „Marke?“, „Geld?“. Keep the modelTurns, which are already personal questions.
findings.proposedRule: EXM-04: for interaction 'cards-ask' on ga2.sp1, a card is one keyword ending in '?', with no ':' topic prefix and no Thema in situationDe.

findings.quote: "template":"ga2.h3", "scaffolded":false, options ["einen weißen","einen roten","einen schwarzen"]
findings.problem: In Goethe A2 Hören Teil 3 the answer options are pictures (BLUEPRINT §4.9 names „Goethe A2 Hören 2 and 3“ as pictorial). Until images exist, a .1 course runs it only as the text variant, with scaffolded: true and labelled „In der Prüfung mit Bildern“. This block uses text options, says scaffolded: false and has no label, so the learner is not told the exam shows pictures. EXM-02 passed only because ga2.h3 lacks pictorial: true (see the registry finding below).
findings.fix: Set scaffolded: true on the block and show the „In der Prüfung mit Bildern“ label. No content change is needed.
findings.proposedRule: EXM-02 already covers this once ga2.h2/ga2.h3 carry pictorial: true.

findings.quote: ga2.l2/ga2.h3/ga2.sp1 have scaffoldAllowedIn ['a2.1'] but no `scaffold`, no `pictorial`, no `instructionsDe`/`paraphraseOf`
findings.problem: This is a gate hole. SCHEMA §4.3 requires `scaffold` limits whenever scaffoldAllowedIn ≠ [], and `pictorial` on every template. Without them EXM-01/TXT-02 cannot check reduced blocks: the 71-word Wegweiser passed against the 100–270 band. EXM-02 also cannot enforce the text-variant rule, so the H3 flag above passed.
findings.fix: Lane owner: add pictorial (h2, h3 true), scaffold {minItems, textWords, playsFixed, optionsFixed} and the paraphrased instructionsDe/paraphraseOf to every ga2 template. Then have validate fail when a template with scaffoldAllowedIn ≠ [] lacks scaffold.
findings.proposedRule: REF/EXM: a TeilTemplate with non-empty scaffoldAllowedIn must define scaffold; every TeilTemplate must define pictorial (boolean).

findings.quote: Kaufhaus am Markt – Wegweiser … (71 words)
findings.problem: The Wegweiser has 71 words. ga2.l2 sets textWords 100–270 (official sample ≈ 120). The level plan (a2-1.md E4) says this is „the first text at ≈ 85 % of official length (≈ 200 words)“. With five short lines the learner never has to scan a crowded directory, which is the real skill in L2, and the „a word appears twice“ strategy has almost nothing to act on.
findings.fix: Expand to ≈ 150–200 words. Give each floor 5–8 entries, add a Restaurant/Café, Kasse/Toiletten, a Kinderwelt entry, and a second 'Kundenservice' or 'Information' line on another floor so the trap in item 03 has company. Keep all four keys valid (Kinderkleidung only on 2, Gläser only on 3, Reparaturen only on 4, Kabel only in EG). A fifth item would make the block full length.

findings.quote: „Eine Jacke für ein Kind finden Sie bei „Kleidung für Kinder“.“
findings.problem: The strategy card for the block gives away the answer to exam item a2.1-u04-ls4-ga2-l2-01 („Ihr Sohn braucht eine Jacke für den Winter.“ → 2. Stockwerk). The item then measures nothing. It also teaches the reverse of the strategy it names: the learner is handed the category instead of inferring it.
findings.fix: Use an example that no item uses, e.g. „Einen Teller finden Sie bei „Geschirr“.“ or „Einen Schrank finden Sie bei „Möbel“.“
findings.proposedRule: ITM: a strategy card's example must not contain the key-bearing noun phrase of any item in the same step.

findings.quote: cd.a2.alltagsdinge-bewerten: „Ich kann kurz sagen, wie mir … ein Gerät gefällt und was ich daran gut oder nicht so gut finde.“ (productive-spoken)
findings.problem: This can-do is claimed but never rehearsed as a task. No microOutput asks the learner to evaluate a device: LS1 asks what you are looking for and the price, LS2 is about lending a Föhn, LS3 is the complaint. The Sprechen proof is a Fragen-zur-Person exchange in which evaluating comes up at most in one answer (partner card „Marke?“), and the ga2-sp1 rubric does not score it. Redemittel rm04 „Ich finde das Modell sehr praktisch.“ is never required.
findings.fix: Change the LS2 microOutput (or add a second prompt line to LS1's): „Priya zeigt Ihnen zwei Kaffeemaschinen. Wie finden Sie sie? Was ist gut, was nicht so gut?“, spoken, course-micro-sp, target g.adj-dekl-unbestimmt + g.komparation. Point the proof for cd.a2.alltagsdinge-bewerten to that microOutput instead of the Sprechen Teil.
findings.proposedRule: ALL-02: a productive can-do's proof must be a task whose prompt names the can-do's function (bewerten/sagen, wie … gefällt), not only an exam Teil whose rubric does not score it.

findings.quote: „„Gibt es da auch eins?“ Was sucht Arjun?“ options [ein Modell, eine Kaffeemaschine, einen Föhn], key „ein Modell“ · „„Wir brauchen nur eine.“ Was brauchen sie?“ options [eine Kaffeemaschine, einen Wasserkocher, ein Gerät]
findings.problem: Each item has a distractor that is true by meaning. Arjun is looking for a coffee machine online, so „eine Kaffeemaschine“ answers „Was sucht Arjun?“ correctly. They need exactly one device, so „ein Gerät“ answers „Was brauchen sie?“. The key follows only from form (eins = neuter), but the question asks about content. A learner who understood the dialogue is marked wrong.
findings.fix: Ask about form: „Wofür steht „eins“?“ / „Wofür steht „eine“?“. Replace the hypernym distractors with nouns of the wrong gender that are not true by meaning: s02 options [ein Modell, eine Marke, einen Föhn] (Marke is in l03); s03 options [eine Kaffeemaschine, einen Wasserkocher, ein Kabel].
findings.proposedRule: ITM-02: in a 'structured' referent item (a pronoun → which noun), no distractor may be a hypernym or hyponym of the key's referent in the input.

findings.quote: „Haben wir noch Tassen? – Ja, wir haben ___.“ answer „welche“, accepted [„welche“]
findings.problem: This is an open fill-in without a German cue. „viele“ and „genug“ are correct, natural answers („Ja, wir haben viele.“) and are marked wrong. Only the English line („Pronoun for a plural noun“) points to welche, and ITM-01 requires the German prompt to decide.
findings.fix: Make it multiple_choice with options [welche, eine, eins] (the r04 shape), or keep the fill-in and change the prompt to „… – Ja, wir haben noch ___. (die Tassen → Pronomen)“. Do not just widen accepted[].

findings.quote: „Ist hier ein Aufzug? – Ja, dort ist ___. (der Aufzug)“ accepted [„einer“]
findings.problem: „Ja, dort ist er.“ is idiomatic spoken German for a uniquely identifiable lift. The cue „(der Aufzug)“ does not exclude it.
findings.fix: Change the question to „Gibt es hier einen Aufzug? – Ja, dort ist ___.“, where „einer“ is the natural answer, or change the cue to „(ein Aufzug → Pronomen)“.

findings.quote: l05 „Ja, hier ist eins für 79 Euro, und es ist weiß.“ → i03 „Im Internet kostet das Modell aus der Schweiz ___ Euro.“
findings.problem: The dialogue never says the 79-euro offer is the Swiss model. The key is reached by inference („eins“ = das Modell) or by elimination, and the explicit link only comes in LS3's order e-mail.
findings.fix: l05: „Ja, das Modell aus der Schweiz gibt es online für 79 Euro, und es ist weiß.“ Keep l04 „Gibt es da auch eins?“ as the pronoun model.

findings.quote: „Bitte bezahlen Sie in 14 Tagen.“ · „Die Marke hat eine gute Qualität.“ · „Die Lieferzeit ist nur drei Tage.“ · „Die Zahlung ist dann auf Rechnung.“
findings.problem: Four model-surface phrasings a German shop or salesperson would not use. „in 14 Tagen“ means 'in 14 days' time', not 'within'. „hat eine gute Qualität“ has an odd article. „Lieferzeit ist drei Tage“ is colloquial. „Die Zahlung ist auf Rechnung“ is not idiomatic. In t6 an order is placed with the „Kundenservice“, which usually handles complaints.
findings.fix: „Sie haben 14 Tage Zeit.“ · „Die Marke hat gute Qualität.“ / „Die Qualität ist sehr gut.“ · „Die Lieferung dauert nur drei Tage.“ · „Dann zahlen Sie auf Rechnung.“ Optionally t6 l01 „Bestellservice, guten Tag.“

findings.quote: „Wegweiser: „EG Taschen · 1. Stockwerk Sport · 2. Stockwerk Haushalt“. Wo sind Staubsauger?“
findings.problem: The unit's own Kaufhaus am Markt has Haushalt on the 3rd floor, Taschen on the 1st and Sport on the 2nd (LS1 l02, LS4 t1, c05). The proof item's sign contradicts the store the learner just studied, and a learner who remembers „3. Stockwerk“ finds no matching option.
findings.fix: Name a different store („Wegweiser im Kaufhaus Lindner: …“) or align the floors with Kaufhaus am Markt and use options [im 3. Stockwerk, im 2. Stockwerk, im Erdgeschoss].

findings.quote: „Wir brauchen die Kaffeemaschine bis Samstag. Meine Eltern kommen.“ · „Ihre Freundin Anna schreibt: „Hast du einen Föhn für mich?““
findings.problem: Two small story breaks. (1) The visit of Arjun's parents (from Kochi) is a new cast fact that appears nowhere in series.json or the plan and is never followed up. The cliffhanger moves to Anna's birthday. (2) LS2 has just said that Anna HAS a Föhn and Priya needs one, yet the microOutput has Anna asking for one.
findings.fix: (1) Use a reason that needs no cast fact: „Am Samstag kommen Anna und Felix zum Frühstück.“ That also sets up E5. (2) Make the requester Priya: „Ihre Freundin Priya schreibt: „Hast du einen Föhn für mich? Meiner ist kaputt.““

findings.quote: aiRole Marta = „Teilnehmerin in der Prüfung“ · openingLine „Guten Tag! Wir beginnen mit Teil 1. Stellen Sie bitte Ihre erste Frage.“ · „Welche Marke finden Sie gut?“ → „Ich habe eine Kaffeemaschine aus der Schweiz. Die Marke finde ich sehr gut.“
findings.problem: The opening line is an examiner's line, spoken by a fellow candidate. The model answer to „Welche Marke …?“ names no brand, so it does not answer the question. A learner copying it would lose Aufgabenerfüllung.
findings.fix: Opening: „Hallo, ich bin Marta. Fangen Sie an?“ (or give the line to a separate examiner voice). Model answer: „Ich kaufe gern Geräte aus der Schweiz. Die Qualität ist sehr gut.“ Or change the card to „Geräte?“ with the question „Welche Geräte kaufen Sie gern?“

findings.quote: „Sie hören fünf kurze Gespräche. Sie hören jeden Text einmal. Wählen Sie a, b oder c.“ · „… In welches Stockwerk gehen Sie? Wählen Sie a, b oder c.“
findings.problem: Both instructions follow the official Goethe A2 wording almost verbatim. LGL-05 / SCHEMA §4.3 ask for our own paraphrase, never the official wording. The risk is low because the sentences are functional, but the rule is binding and the ga2 templates carry no paraphrase to copy from.
findings.fix: Paraphrase, e.g. „Fünf kurze Gespräche – jedes nur einmal. Welche Antwort passt: a, b oder c?“ and „Wo finden Sie das? Wählen Sie das Stockwerk: a, b oder c.“ The lane owner should add instructionsDe/paraphraseOf to the templates (see the registry finding).
findings.proposedRule: LGL-05 n-gram check of block instructionsDe against the official instruction strings.

findings.quote: „Ich gehe jeden Samstag in den Supermarkt.“ · „Sie braucht die Mikrowelle jeden Tag.“ · „das passende Wort“
findings.problem: Small look-aheads. jeden + accusative time phrase is g.zeitangaben-akkusativ (a2.1-u07), and it appears in a model turn the learner imitates. „das passende Wort“ is g.adj-dekl-bestimmt (u05) in an instruction. Both are common chunks, so the effect is small.
findings.fix: Model turn: „Ich gehe am Samstag in den Supermarkt.“ Strategy card: „… suchen Sie dann das Wort im Wegweiser.“ Leave „jeden Tag“ in the receptive exam text, or mark it as a chunk.

findings.quote: p08 „einen steht für einen Föhn“ (no Föhn in the prompt) · r03 errorTags [„spelling-meaning“] on a superlative word-order item · i04 „Das Modell für 65 Euro ist am ___.“ accepted [„günstigsten“]
findings.problem: The p08 explanation refers to an antecedent the item never shows. The r03 error tag does not match what the item tests. i04 is heard, not quoted, so „billigsten“ is a correct superlative for the same meaning and is marked wrong.
findings.fix: p08 prompt: „Bilden Sie die Antwort: Hat jemand einen Föhn?“, or make the explanation generic. Set r03's errorTags to [] or to a word-order tag. Change i04's prompt to „Priya sagt: Das Modell für 65 Euro ist am ___.“ plus a word cue, or add „billigsten“ with acceptedWhy.

findings.quote: q03 multiple_choice „Was fragen Sie im Geschäft?“ proves an interaction-spoken can-do
findings.problem: The can-do is proven by recognising the right question. The unit does rehearse it productively, in the LS1 spoken microOutput („Fragen Sie nach dem Preis“), but the proof does not point there.
findings.fix: Point the proof at the LS1 microOutput (a2.1-u04-ls1-mo) and add „und nach der Garantie oder der Farbe“ to its prompt. Keep q03 as a supporting check item.

findings.quote: TXT-03 advisory: input ≈ 52 s (need 60–120 s)
findings.problem: The LS3 listening part is short of the input minimum. The e-mail carries most of the step's input.
findings.fix: Add 2–3 lines, e.g. Priya reads out the returns part of the e-mail and Arjun asks when the Kundenservice is open (8–18 Uhr). This also exercises alltagstexte-durchsuchen.

findings.quote: GRM-04 det.konjunktiv1 flags „Nachmittag gehe“, „Samstag arbeite“, „Wohnung wohne“, „Marke finde“
findings.problem: All four are false positives: first-person singular present indicative after a fronted element (Heute Nachmittag gehe ich …). The detector cannot tell them from Konjunktiv I, so it will fire in every unit that has inversion with ich.
findings.fix: Detector owner: require a 3rd-person subject (er/sie/es/man/NP) or a -e form that differs from the indicative (sei, habe with 3sg, komme with er) before flagging. No change in u04.
findings.proposedRule: det.konjunktiv1 fixture: „Am Samstag arbeite ich.“ must not match.

findings.quote: LEX-02 ratchet: „Vorteil“ … „Lieferzeit“ recur in 0 later unit(s) (need ≥ 2)
findings.problem: No later a2.1 unit exists yet, so this is a measurement of absence, not a defect in u04. Recorded so the ratchet (28) is re-measured once u05–u12 exist.
findings.fix: No change to u04. When writing u05–u12, recycle the unit's words (Lieferung, Rücksendung, günstig, vergleichen, Marke, Qualität, Vorteil are natural in E5 and E11).

itemsSolvedBlind.note: All adjective-ending, pronoun, sentence-building and exam keys are correct. Every sentence-building tile set yields exactly the accepted orders.

examCheck.ga2.l2: abc, 3 options with „anderes Stockwerk“ as c, reduced to 4 of 5 items and scaffolded: true (allowed in a2.1). Text 71 words, below the 100–270 band. Items are original (the official MS item is the watch battery).
examCheck.ga2.h3: 5 dialogues of 45–55 words (band 35–75), 5 items, 3 options, played once. The pictorial text-variant flag is missing.
examCheck.ga2.s2: Halbformell e-mail, 3 Leitpunkte, 30–40 words, rubric ga2-s2, examKey goethe_a2. Model text is 37 words. Feasible at A2.1. Original (the MS task is an e-mail to the boss).
examCheck.ga2.sp1: cards-ask, prep 0, 4 + 4 cards, rubric ga2-sp1. The card layout is themed like SD1/telc A2 rather than Goethe A2 „Fragen zur Person“.
